seoTitle: Insights for software M&A | Capital Row
seoDescription: Sourced research for buyers, owners and lenders in vertical software: the market, why deals break, origination costs, diligence findings and SBA rules.

sections.name: What the record shows, before the letter of intent.

items.text: What the record shows, before the letter of intent.

Research notes on the lower middle market in vertical software: where the deals are, why the signed ones die, what it costs to originate one, and what a buyer’s diligence will find. Every figure on these pages is sourced, and the sources are listed under it.

sections.name: The market, and what it costs to see it.

items.text: The market, and what it costs to see it.
The market is busy. Most of it goes unseen.
2,784 SaaS transactions in twelve months, more than half of them vertical software, and the median private equity firm saw fewer than one in five of the deals inside its own stated market.

Ten deals that were signed and then died, or were cut in price before closing, told from court opinions, filings and announcements.
